title: Al Hamra Tower
visualBrief: Kuwait’s sculpted tower with a fixed rounded glass envelope, southwest-to-southeast moving courtyard cut, two continuous limestone flares, deep angled south-wall windows, sloping east blade and24m lamella-framed north entrance.

reconstruction.massing: The architect’s published five sections establish a fixed filleted square with the removed quarter moving from southwest at ground level to southeast at the top. The model reconstructs that moving cut and its two ruled stone walls rather than rotating the entire tower.
reconstruction.facade: Completed SOM exterior photographs establish blue north/east/west glazing, thin horizontal metal rails, a warm limestone south wall and small deeply splayed openings. The eighty-row aperture schedule and detailed reveal depths are photograph reconstructions.
reconstruction.crown: The east-facing blade reaches412.6m while the western edge is lower. A closed inclined roof follows the same concave outline; the40m upper hall is represented by its exterior envelope.
reconstruction.entry: Primary lobby plan and photographs establish the northern entrance,24m inclined lamella structure and curved metal canopy supports. The separate southern shopping mall and eastern parking block are excluded.

geographicProposal.orientationConfidence: exact mapped identity plus north-arrow architect site/lobby plans and cut sections

scaleBasis: Published owner/architect/contractor heights and distinguishing construction systems; map footprint for local orientation, with reconstructed details declared separately.
geometrySource: Original deterministic exterior geometry; no downloaded meshes or copied photographic textures. Footprint-derived registration includes separately attributed OpenStreetMap evidence.
sourceLicense: Original reconstruction under repository license. Map-derived plan evidence: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications are linked, not redistributed.
materialMethod: Canonical shared material graphs bound through molenSurface extras with metric coordinates divided by central repeat meters. Vertex colors provide component tint. Glass retains opaque metallic-roughness PBR; no bitmap texture copies per model.
reviewStatus: source-geometry; near/far and shared-material captures pending
limitations: Original 155029-triangle, 18088600-byte master remains exactly reproducible from the unchanged original recipe. Reviewed source and four browser levels keep the fixed filleted glass envelope, continuously moving southern courtyard, two ruled limestone flares, deeply angled south-wall windows, inclined closed roof/east blade, 24 m north lamella and supported canopy. Whole backing panels with long trim strips replace independent framed cells; adjacent stone windows share continuous piers. Skyline averages thin glazing trim, omits individual apertures/door frames/hidden lamella and makes lobby glazing opaque. District uses twenty south-window rows/six columns and aggregates thin trim; street retains all 960 deeply splayed openings but aggregates facade rails; close-up restores finer rails and curved canopy branches. Canonical limestone approximates Jura/trencadis; painted metal approximates canopy stainless to share the glazing-trim graph. Near lobby and canopy clear glass uses distinct explicit portable/runtime references and a single transparent group, required to see the lamella; other glazing is opaque. Fixed non-planar roof triangulation is shared across levels; sampled ruled flares retain courtyard geometry. Far copings use flat strips. Canopy support bases are repaired from mistaken size-as-bounds arguments. Exact fillet radius, window schedule/reveal depth, lamella members, parapet profile and canopy dimensions are reconstructions from published photos/plans. Designer 74, Architectural Record 77 and CTBUH 80 storeys use different counts and remain recorded; 412.6 m top and 351.2 m occupied heights follow CTBUH. Mall, parking block, interior fittings, signage and animated lighting are excluded. Finite along-ray allowances 1.5/.75/.3/.1 m exclude thin mullions, coping edges and omitted/aggregated district apertures; they are not global surface-distance bounds. No physical-device or surveyed grade claim.
importReason: Preserve thin facade frames, panel joints and crown/antenna details until a measured LOD chain is authored.
